title: Square-zero kernel of the tensor graded algebra quotient
statement: Given a closed immersion j:Z→X, an invertible module L, the graded algebra coproduct data A [lem-sc-tensor-graded-algebra-data], and j.ker²=0 [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], every product of two local sections of ker(A.p) is zero, on every open subset of X.

source.place: Tag 09MS, coherent-equation-ses and its direct sum; canonical construction before cohomology

proof.text: Apply the local ideal-generation lemma at each point to put both kernel sections on a common affine neighborhood in the extension of j.ker. Evaluate hI on this affine open to obtain J(V)*J(V)=0. Mathlib Ideal.mul_mem_mul and Ideal.map_mul show that the product of the two sections is zero after restriction. The separation clause of the sheaf condition proves it is zero on the original open.

mathlib_searches.query: The direct sum of tensor powers of an invertible sheaf is a commutative algebra sheaf with a square zero quotient kernel
In an abelian category with exact coproducts the coproduct of kernels is the kernel of a coproduct of morphisms

lean.statement: theorem tensorGradedKernel_squareZero {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (A : TensorGradedAlgebraData j L) (hI : j.ker ^ 2 = ⊥) : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (a b : A.B.right.obj.obj (op U)), A.p.right.hom.app (op U) a = 0 → A.p.right.hom.app (op U) b = 0 → a * b = 0
